items.title: Nobel physics winner's pride at pioneering AI role
items.excerpt: Nobel laureate Francis Halzen recalled his early push for AI in neutrino research, including a 1991 paper proposing it for particle-physics data. Neural networks later helped IceCube pull the Milky Way out of its neutrino data.

items.title: AI chatbots endorse existing climate-related policies twice as often as new proposals
items.excerpt: University of Waterloo researchers tested 11 LLMs on 7,500+ queries: chatbots endorsed existing plans about 70% of the time versus 34% for new ones, and under-recommended EVs relative to actual sales (Environmental Research Communications).

items.title: Unlocking AI as a research tool for plant microscopy
items.excerpt: University of Queensland's PlantMicro benchmark shows vision-language models identify plant hosts and diseases from microscopy images with only ~30% accuracy (ECCV 2026).

items.title: A new approach to sustainable AI: Offloading part of the computational burden onto light
items.excerpt: Koç University photonic systems move part of AI processing onto light: a programmable optical neural network lifted skin-lesion classification from 68% to 98%, and a multimode fiber laser hit 85-99% accuracy with fewer trainable parameters (Communications Engineering / Communications Physics).
items.note: time from Science X RSS pubDate; page shows date only

items.title: AI helps identify drilling regimes with a projected potential increase in drilling speed of up to 68%
items.excerpt: Skoltech combined machine learning, explainable AI and multi-objective optimization to find drilling settings balancing speed, torque and energy in carbonate reservoirs; one well projected a 68.4% faster penetration rate (Results in Engineering).

items.title: AI behaves more like a brain than a database—cognitive science's role in its origin story helps explain why
items.excerpt: Cognitive scientists Michael Hout and Arryn Robbins trace modern AI's lineage to psychology and brain-inspired learning, explaining why it generates fluent but sometimes wrong answers rather than retrieving stored facts.

items.title: legoESM: a modular, differentiable, multiscale, AI-ready Earth system model built with AI agents
items.excerpt: legoESM is a composable, differentiable Earth system model in JAX, recast from decades of community parameterizations by AI coding agents under a human-specified scientific contract, targeting cloud-feedback uncertainty in climate response.

items.title: Is Your AI Fast Enough to Run a Fusion Reactor?
items.excerpt: Lessons from ML models deployed for control on the DIII-D tokamak plus a benchmark of ten fusion control/diagnostic networks: above five million parameters CPU backends take tens to thousands of ms, setting a limit for real-time plasma control.
items.note: preprint; no og:image; PACMAN/DIII-D covered 2026-09-03, different angle

items.title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation Algorithms
items.excerpt: An LLM agent rewrites the Sella geometry optimizer to cut DFT force-call counts in quantum-chemistry workflows, gated against premature stopping and non-generalizing gains on unseen molecules.

items.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
items.excerpt: Mathematicians are facing AI's sudden advance with grief, anger and a search for fresh ideas: 'If we don't adapt, there's just no more math in 50 years.'
items.note: math-provers axis deprioritized; Unique Games piece already published

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for monitoring and protecting wildlife around the world.

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Psychologists apply attachment theory, the framework for the relationships that hold lives together, to explain how and why people bond with AI companions.

items.title: What makes a good AI safety test? Experts explain why even the best techniques may not be powerful enough
items.excerpt: Researchers explain the science of AI evaluations: 'With today's science we usually can't show with high confidence that dangerous behavior isn't there.'

items.title: How AI helped bring an ancient tomb dating to before the Roman Empire back to life
items.excerpt: Pairing artificial intelligence with acoustic technology let archaeoacousticians reconstruct how the Etruscan Tomb of the Blue Demons sounded.

items.title: How AI Is Influencing Language and Meaning
items.excerpt: AI-speak is changing how we use words, introducing new terms and altering the meaning of familiar ones.

items.title: Does better work always mean better workers?
items.excerpt: In a three-month RCT with practicing patent attorneys (David Autor et al.), routine AI use lifted work quality across the board; senior lawyers gained stronger judgment while juniors showed no average skill gain, their scores polarizing.
items.note: date-only on page; human-AI reliance axis deprioritized (persistence study ran 10-10)

items.title: OpenAI claims we've entered the AGI era — has GPT-6 Astra really demonstrated general intelligence?
items.excerpt: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra brings humanity to the threshold of AGI, but external evaluators argue inflated lab metrics and opaque testing obscure its true reliability.
